title: Mongolia’s New Government Set Ambitious Goals. But Are They Realistic?
gist: Mongolia's parliament opened its autumn session on Sept 15, 2026, facing PM Uchral Nyam-Osor's ambitious agenda including one of the largest state budgets, a sovereign wealth fund, energy imports from China and data centers. The author questions feasibility given political division and instability since June 2025.

insights.claim: Mongolia's government under Prime Minister Uchral Nyam-Osor has proposed one of the country's largest state budgets alongside plans for a sovereign wealth fund, securing energy from China and building data centers.
insights.speaker: Bolor Lkhaajav
insights.so_what: Signals Mongolia's push to monetize resources and pivot to digital infrastructure, with China energy dependence rising.

insights.claim: Mongolia has suffered government instability since Oyun-Erdene Luvsannamsrai's administration was ousted in June 2025, and Uchral's government took office only on March 31, 2026.
insights.speaker: Bolor Lkhaajav
insights.so_what: Frequent government turnover raises execution and policy risk for investors in Mongolian mining and infrastructure.

insights.claim: The State Great Khural operates in a highly politically divided environment and will likely scrutinize the government's big initiatives, casting doubt on whether they are realistic.
insights.speaker: Bolor Lkhaajav
insights.so_what: Expect delays or dilution of the sovereign wealth fund and data center plans.
insights.quote: Parliament will likely scrutinize many of these big initiatives.
